follow @poplurst for fascinating psychology, relatable thoughts, human behavior, and the little things about life that make you say, “wait… why is this actually true?” 😭

having a crush on someone who is genuinely smart can have a funny side effect: you suddenly become interested in becoming a better version of yourself. 😂

it’s not necessarily because the person is directly telling you to change. Sometimes, simply being impressed by someone’s intelligence, discipline, ambition, or the way they carry themselves can make you look at your own life differently. Research on admiration has found that admiring someone can motivate people to emulate qualities they value and push themselves toward self-improvement. 

that’s basically the joke behind this meme. One minute you’re simply thinking, “wow, he’s really smart,” and the next minute you’re reading books, fixing your sleep schedule, learning new skills, becoming more disciplined and questioning every decision you’ve made since 2019. 😭

psychologists also describe attraction as something that can strongly activate our emotions and attention. When we’re attracted to someone, our bodies and minds can become unusually focused on that person, which helps explain why a crush can suddenly make everything feel more intense. 

so technically, the meme is exaggerating for comedy, but there’s a real psychological idea underneath it: sometimes admiration makes you want to grow. The dangerous part is when your crush is so impressive that you accidentally turn the attraction into a full personal-development project. 😂💔

🎬 My Own Private Idaho (1991) …

Directed by Gus Van Sant, My Own Private Idaho follows two young street hustlers navigating life, identity, and friendship in the Pacific Northwest.

The story centers on Mike Waters (River Phoenix), a sensitive, narcoleptic young man who suffers from sudden blackouts. He’s searching for his estranged mother, holding onto the hope that finding her will give his life meaning. Mike’s closest companion is Scott Favor (Keanu Reeves), the rebellious son of a wealthy mayor. Scott lives on the streets by choice, planning to inherit his fortune once he turns 21.

Together, they drift through a world of hustling, homelessness, and found family, led loosely by a Shakespearean-inspired mentor figure, Bob Pigeon. While Mike is deeply in love with Scott, Scott doesn’t return those feelings, instead pursuing a more conventional life as he nears adulthood.

Their journey takes them from Portland to Idaho and even to Italy in search of Mike’s mother. Along the way, their bond is tested as Scott begins to abandon street life and Mike confronts the painful reality of his situation.
